title: Confit Chicken Legs
subtitle: Slow-cooked chicken legs in olive oil with garlic and herbs
excerpt: Confit is a French technique where meat is cooked very slowly submerged in fat at a low temperature. It produces extraordinarily tender, richly flavoured meat that can be crisped up in a hot pan just before serving. Chicken legs are a brilliant substitute for the traditional duck.
sourceNotes: Confit is a centuries-old French preservation technique from the Gascony region. Duck confit is the most famous version, but the same low-and-slow method works superbly with chicken legs.

recipe.freezeNotes: Store the cooked legs submerged in their cooking oil in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months. Crisp in a pan straight from cold.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to scale up. Use a roasting tin big enough to hold the legs in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The legs can be cooked up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated in their oil. Crisp the skin in a hot frying pan for 8 to 10 minutes before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 130C / Gas 2. The oil should barely shiver, not simmer.

content.text: The key is keeping the temperature low. If the oil simmers, the chicken steams rather than confits and the texture will be wrong. Check the oven temperature with a probe if you have one. The legs should be fully submerged in oil, so choose a roasting tin that fits them snugly.
Heat the oven to 150C (fan 130C / gas 2). Season the chicken legs generously with salt and pepper.
Place the legs in a snug roasting tin. Tuck the garlic, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves around them. Pour over the olive oil so the legs are mostly submerged. Top up with a little more oil if needed.
Cover tightly with foil and cook in the oven for 2 hours. The oil should barely move during cooking.
Remove from the oven. Lift the legs out carefully and pat the skin dry with kitchen paper.
Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat until very hot. Place the legs skin-side down and cook for 6 to 8 minutes without moving until the skin is deep golden and very crisp. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Skin won't crisp in the pan
items.cause: Skin is still wet from the oil.
items.fix: Pat very dry and use a very hot, dry pan.

items.symptom: Oil bubbled and simmered in the oven
items.fix: Lower the temperature and cover tightly next time.
